title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page holds one programmatic note in the upper right corner, possibly a heading for a planned section. It reads: "Corps de classes commutatif = Motifs à groupes fondamentaux motiviques [?] commutatifs (= Motifs métabéliens)."

In Grothendieck's Tannakian vocabulary, the 'groupe fondamental' of a Tannakian category is its Tannakian (Galois) group. So 'motifs à groupe fondamental motivique commutatif' are motives whose motivic Galois group, or its geometric or identity component, is commutative. The slogan says that abelian class field theory is the theory of exactly these motives.

Modern reading:
- Over an algebraic closure, a motive with commutative connected motivic group has a torus as that group. Such motives are potentially of CM type, generated by CM abelian varieties and Tate twists. The torus is a quotient of the Serre group S.
- Over the ground field k (e.g. Q), the full Galois group of such motives is an extension 1 → (torus) → G → (profinite group) → 1.
- If the finite or Artin part is also restricted to be abelian, G is an extension of an abelian group by a commutative group, i.e. metabelian. This explains the parenthesis '= motifs métabéliens'.
- For k = Q this is precisely the Taniyama group: an extension of Gal(Q^ab/Q) by the Serre torus. It encodes the Shimura–Taniyama reciprocity law for CM abelian varieties together with classical abelian class field theory.

The note thus places class field theory as the 'first layer' of a motivic Galois theory: abelian Galois-type data equals the metabelian part of the motivic Galois group. Implicitly, non-abelian class field theory (Langlands-type) would correspond to general motives.

The previous page is crossed out and illegible; the next page is just the number 157. There is no surrounding derivation.
errors: The equation is a slogan, not a theorem. Commutativity of the connected (geometric) motivic group does not force metabelianity of the full group: Artin motives with non-abelian Galois group have trivial connected component but non-abelian group. 'Métabélien' requires the finite/arithmetic part to be abelian too, as in the Taniyama group over Q.

Identifying motives with commutative connected motivic group with CM motives needs the standard/Hodge-type conjectures, or Deligne's absolute Hodge cycles result for CM abelian varieties. This was unavailable at the time.

ideas.what: Abelian class field theory corresponds to motives whose motivic Galois ('fundamental') group is commutative.
ideas.modern_name: CM motives / Serre group; abelian l-adic representations of algebraic type come from CM motives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Abelian l-adic representations, 1968), Shimura–Taniyama; Deligne, Milne
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck discusses motivic Galois groups in Récoltes et Semailles and letters; this specific class field theory slogan is not known to me in print

ideas.what: The resulting group is metabelian: an extension of an abelian Galois group by a commutative (torus) group.
ideas.modern_name: Taniyama group (extension of Gal(Q^ab/Q) by the Serre group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Langlands (1979, 'Ein Märchen'); Deligne, 'Motifs et groupes de Taniyama' (1982); Milne–Shih

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly frames abelian class field theory as the theory of motives with commutative motivic fundamental group, and calls them 'metabelian motives'. This anticipates the motivic formulation of the Taniyama group as an extension of an abelian Galois group by a torus. The date is uncertain (1965–c.1977), but it is plausibly before Langlands 1979 and Deligne 1982.
missed.quote: Corps de classes commutatif = Motifs à groupes fondamentaux motiviques [...] commutatifs (= Motifs métabéliens).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, it shows Grothendieck viewed class field theory as a stratum of motivic Galois theory, foreshadowing the Taniyama group and the Langlands-motives dictionary. Mathematically the content is now standard, so it matters only for priority and history.

deep.surprise_reason: A terse but conceptually apt slogan that anticipates the Taniyama group viewpoint ('metabelian motives'). The mathematics is now standard (Serre 1968, Langlands/Deligne 1979–82), and the page gives no development. Its interest is mainly historical, and it depends on the uncertain dating.
transcription_corrections: The bracketed word on line 4 is unclear. It may be '[connexes]' rather than '[commutatifs]'. That reading would give 'groupes fondamentaux motiviques [connexes] commutatifs', i.e. connected commutative motivic group, which fits the gloss 'métabéliens' (connected part commutative, plus abelian π0).
First word 'Corps' is consistent with the image ('Corps de classes commutatif' = abelian class field theory).
